div.div:
Tools run inside your own environment
Credentials stay in your environment
Attribution via your service or user API key
Logging executions logged and available for audit
Required when the server is private, on localhost, or otherwise
unreachable from the internet, because a provider cannot reach it
at all. Also the route for Bedrock and Vertex AI, which do not
execute MCP tools remotely.
With the prefix, server_description, server_url and require_approval are ignored if passed.

div.div:
Tools run on provider servers
Credentials tokens may reach provider training data
and audit pipelines
Attribution none
Logging no execution logging, no security controls
The gateway sees the request and the final answer. It does not
see the tool call, so nothing about that call reaches your logs,
your guardrails, or your audit trail.

div.div:
To avoid leaking keys, the Responses API stores the value of no string you put in
the headers object, and those values never appear in the response object.
Because some servers hand out authenticated URLs, the path of server_url is
discarded too: example.com/mcp comes back as example.com.
The consequence is operational. Every single request must carry the full
server_url path and every header again. Code that sets them once and
reuses a stored response will fail on the second call, usually with a 404.

div.div:
A server registered in the MCP Registry can also be used from the inference
path, by pointing server_url at its gateway address:
https://aigw.portkey.ai/m/<slug>/mcp
No auth or header auth pass the gateway API key as
x-portkey-api-key inside the headers object.
OAuth servers pass the token in the authorization field on the tool.
These bodies carry a plain server_label, so they are provider execution
and the right-hand column above applies. Prefixing the label keeps
execution on the gateway.

div.div:
Gateway execution is the default answer for an enterprise. It keeps tool execution and credentials inside your environment, attributes the call to a key you
issued, and leaves an audit trail. Provider execution exists because it is simpler and because some providers support it natively, and it is a reasonable choice
for a public, unauthenticated server where none of those three properties matters.
The decision is not reversible by configuration alone. It lives in the request body your applications send, so changing it later means changing code and
redeploying. Settle it before application teams build against either shape.
Gateway execution is a beta feature. The header carries a date, server-side-mcp-2026-06-01, so the shape may change. Confirm it still applies before
committing a customer to it.
